items.title: Claude Opus 5: Benchmarks, Pricing, and New Effort Mode Explained
items.summary: Matthew Berman covers the launch of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, reviewing its benchmark performance versus Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6. He walks through the new effort mode settings — low, medium, high, and xhigh — that let users trade off cost against reasoning depth. The model launches at the same $5/$25 per million token pricing as Opus 4.8, with a 1M-token context window.
items.whyItMatters: Opus 5 gives developers near-Fable-5 intelligence at half the price, making long-context agentic tasks significantly more affordable. The effort mode is a new lever for balancing cost and capability at inference time.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the API pricing for Claude Opus 5 at launch?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Anthropic kept Claude Opus 5 pricing equal to its predecessor Opus 4.8 at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, despite the capability improvements.

knowledgeChecks.question: What new inference-time control does Claude Opus 5 introduce?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Opus 5 introduces an effort mode setting that lets users specify how much compute the model should expend — from low (fast and cheap) to xhigh (maximum reasoning depth) — allowing cost-capability tradeoffs at inference time.

items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5 With Improved Coding, Safety, and Agent Capabilities
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, positioning it as a near-Fable-5 model at roughly half the cost. The model tops Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA on coding and knowledge tasks, and is Anthropic's safest model to date — with lower rates of deceptive behavior and hard-to-reverse errors versus predecessors. Beta features include mid-conversation tool updates without resetting prompt caches and automatic fallback routing when safety classifiers flag a request.
items.whyItMatters: Opus 5 pushes Anthropic's safety research into a production frontier model, combining top coding performance with quantifiably safer behavior — a combination that matters most for autonomous agent deployments.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which benchmarks did Claude Opus 5 top at launch?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: According to Anthropic's launch coverage, Opus 5 placed at the top of Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA for coding and knowledge tasks, outperforming Claude Fable 5 on a number of benchmarks.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens when Opus 5's safety classifiers flag a request on the API?
options: The request is blocked and returns an error
The model asks the user for clarification
The request is automatically routed to an available model instead
The model attempts the request with reduced capability
knowledgeChecks.explanation: A new beta feature automatically routes requests flagged by Opus 5's safety classifiers to another available model instead of simply blocking the request — reducing friction while maintaining safety guardrails.

items.title: Claude Opus 5 Achieves Near-Zero Prompt Injection Rate for Browser Agents Using Auto Mode
items.summary: Researchers testing Claude Opus 5 with Anthropic's Auto Mode found a 0% prompt injection success rate across 129 test scenarios for browser-based AI agents — a major improvement on the 3.7% baseline rate without Auto Mode protections. Auto Mode stacks two independent defense layers: the first scans incoming data for hidden instructions before the model processes it, and the second blocks dangerous actions before execution. An attacker must defeat both layers independently to succeed.
items.whyItMatters: Browser-based prompt injection has been the most dangerous open vulnerability for AI agents operating on the web. A near-zero attack success rate — if it holds in production — would remove the biggest blocker to deploying autonomous agents that browse the web on users' behalf.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is Claude Opus 5's prompt injection success rate in 129 browser agent test scenarios when using Auto Mode?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: With Auto Mode enabled, Opus 5 achieved a 0% prompt injection success rate across 129 test scenarios. Without Auto Mode's layered defenses, the baseline rate is 3.7%.

knowledgeChecks.question: How many independent defense layers does Opus 5's Auto Mode stack against prompt injection?
options: Two — input scanning and action blocking
Three — input scan, sandboxing, and output filter
Four — rate limiting plus three content layers
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Auto Mode layers two independent defenses: one scans incoming data for hidden instructions before the model processes them, and the second blocks dangerous actions before execution. Both must be beaten independently for an attack to succeed.

items.title: Anthropic Publishes New Context Engineering Rules for Claude 5 Generation Models
items.summary: Anthropic's engineering team published updated context engineering best practices coinciding with the Claude Opus 5 launch, revealing that they removed over 80% of Claude Code's internal system prompt for Opus 5 and Fable 5 with no measurable loss on coding evaluations. The post argues the cuts worked by removing constraints that once prevented worst-case behavior but now create conflicting instructions and wasted tokens in more capable models. Key recommendations: place project rules close to the repository, encode repeatable workflows as skills or local instructions, and keep prompts short and task-specific.
items.whyItMatters: Developers building on Claude 5 models can dramatically reduce prompt complexity without sacrificing performance — a finding that challenges the conventional wisdom of packing system prompts with detailed instructions and that has direct implications for agent cost and reliability.

knowledgeChecks.question: What percentage of Claude Code's system prompt did Anthropic remove for Claude 5 generation models?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Anthropic removed over 80% of Claude Code's internal system prompt when moving to Opus 5 and Fable 5 models, with no measurable loss on coding evaluations — demonstrating that many prior constraints became counterproductive as models grew more capable.

knowledgeChecks.question: According to Anthropic's context engineering guide, what is the main reason verbose system prompts hurt performance in Claude 5 models?
options: They exceed the context window token limit
They create conflicting instructions and waste tokens that once constrained worst cases
They prevent the model from accessing long-term memory
They reduce the model's ability to call external tools
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The guide explains that constraints which once prevented worst-case outputs in earlier models now create conflicting instructions and wasted tokens in Claude 5 generation models, actively degrading performance rather than improving safety.

items.title: Kimi K3 Open Weights Drop July 27: 2.8T-Parameter Model Targets Frontier Coding With Hallucination Caveats
items.summary: Moonshot AI is releasing the full open weights for Kimi K3, its 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, on July 27, 2026, under a Modified MIT license. The model scored 1,679 Elo points on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard — surpassing Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol — and features Kimi Delta Attention for faster decoding plus a 1M-token context window with native vision. TechTimes flags that Moonshot has not disclosed a formal hallucination benchmark, which analysts consider a material omission at this scale.
items.whyItMatters: At 2.8 trillion parameters, Kimi K3 is the largest open-weight model ever released, giving researchers and enterprises frontier-level coding capability that can be self-hosted and fine-tuned — a significant democratization of capability previously locked behind proprietary APIs.

knowledgeChecks.question: What Elo score did Kimi K3 achieve on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Kimi K3 scored 1,679 Elo points on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard, placing it above Claude Fable 5 (1,631) and GPT-5.6 Sol (1,618) — the first Chinese model to hold the top position.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under what license are Kimi K3's open weights being released?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Kimi K3's weights are released under a Modified MIT license, allowing free download, inspection, fine-tuning, and self-hosting for organizations with sufficient infrastructure.
